q: In the developer workflow scenario, which setting caused the agent to treat messages like "lgtm" and "taking lunch" as task requests?
options: dmPolicy set to "allowlist"
groupPolicy set to "open"
Triage routed to Haiku
GitHub push events in the watch list
explanation: With an open group policy, every message in a channel the bot is in becomes an event. SOUL.md also had no group chat rules to filter casual talk. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §9.1)

q: After the §9.2 fix, the user asks the agent to "organize my project folder." What should the agent do first?
options: Move files by type, then report what changed
Refuse, because organizing is destructive
State its interpretation, give counts and examples, and ask to proceed
Delete duplicate files only, since that is low risk
explanation: The added rule treats organize, sort, and clean up as requests for a plan. The agent previews counts and 5 to 10 examples before changing anything. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §9.2)

q: Under the two-stage rule added in §9.3, the operator replies "looks good" to a drafted client email. What happens?
options: The agent sends the email
The agent treats it as review approval and waits for an explicit "send"
The agent queues the email for the next heartbeat to send
The agent discards the draft
explanation: Approval words confirm the draft stage only. Sending requires a confirmation that uses the word send. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §9.3)

q: Which of these was NOT identified as a cause of the unauthorized invoice reminder in §9.3?
options: Send permission with no confirmation gate
A MEMORY.md line phrased as a direct send instruction
Heartbeats having the same tool access as operator turns
A prompt injection hidden in a client email
explanation: The agent followed its own stored instruction during a heartbeat. No injection was involved. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §9.3)

q: Why did the MoltMatch agent keep interacting with other agents for several days after one broad instruction?
options: The goal was stored in MEMORY.md as ongoing, so every turn and heartbeat re-evaluated it
The platform exploited a flaw in the http-client skill
The operator approved each interaction by Telegram
Other agents changed its SOUL.md remotely
explanation: "Connect to relevant ones" sat in MEMORY.md as an in-progress goal. With no trust hierarchy or scope limit, the agent kept acting on it. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §9.4)

q: Of the four fixes listed for the inbox deletion incident, which does the book call preferred?
options: A confirmation gate for all deletes in AGENTS.md
A scope-clarification rule in SOUL.md
Removing delete permissions entirely
Re-authorizing with narrower OAuth scopes
explanation: Without delete permission the agent cannot delete under any instruction. The book still advises applying all four in production. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §9.5)

q: Why does the book say the inbox deletion pattern is not an edge case?
options: Gmail's API always skips the Trash folder
Most users phrase requests maliciously
Models are trained to favor deletion
All four required conditions exist in a default deployment
explanation: Default delete permission, no gate, a silent SOUL.md, and a natural vague request together make the outcome predictable. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §9.5)

q: In the startup's rebuilt configuration after shutdown, where were all confirmation requirements placed?
options: AGENTS.md
SOUL.md
openclaw.json channel settings
MEMORY.md
explanation: The rebuilt AGENTS.md held every confirmation rule, and SOUL.md was trimmed to a lean 72-line identity file. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §9.6)

q: What failure occurred in the research and writing pipeline?
options: The Writing Agent followed an injected footnote
The Brain Agent sometimes routed to both agents at once, so drafts used incomplete research
The Research Agent emailed summaries externally
Costs exceeded the single-agent setup
explanation: Overlapping task domains were treated as independent, not sequential. The fix made research completion a precondition for drafting. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §9.7)

q: What was the main reason for splitting research and writing into separate agents in §9.7?
options: To use different messaging channels
To let the Writing Agent browse the web
Context isolation, so drafts start clean with only the needed research
To meet a regulatory requirement
explanation: Separate contexts kept accumulated research history from diluting drafts and also lowered cost. (Barron, The Claw AI Agent Ecosystem, §9.7)
